name: X-linked Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease Type 1

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for CMTX1

criteria.description: Progressive distal muscle weakness and atrophy predominantly in lower limbs with sensory loss
Intermediate slowing of motor nerve conduction velocities on electrophysiological studies
Identification of pathogenic mutation in the GJB1 gene
X-linked inheritance pattern with affected males and carrier females

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive distal neuropathy with supportive electrophysiological findings and confirmed pathogenic GJB1 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis; nerve conduction studies help differentiate from other CMT types.

common.symptomName: Hyporeflexia or areflexia in distal limbs
Mild to moderate sensory neuropathy symptoms (numbness, tingling)

occasional.symptomName: Transient central nervous system symptoms (e.g., stroke-like episodes)
occasional.notes: More common in males during childhood or adolescence

rare.symptomName: Severe CNS involvement with recurrent transient hemiparesis

imaging: Brain MRI may show transient white matter changes during CNS episodes
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in GJB1 gene encoding connexin 32
other: Nerve conduction studies showing intermediate slowing of motor nerve conduction velocities (30-40 m/s)

redFlags: Rapidly progressive weakness or sensory loss
Early onset CNS symptoms such as stroke-like episodes
references: Bird TD. Charcot-Marie-Tooth Neuropathy Type 1. GeneReviews® [Internet]. 2020.
Lupski JR, et al. Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease: molecular genetics and clinical implications. Neurology. 2010.
Bergoffen J, et al. Connexin mutations in X-linked Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease. Science. 1993.
